issues.description: The solution implementation uses a different attribute/parameter name for the course instructor than the problem statement and template. The problem statement and template refer to the property/initializer label as `instructor`, but the solution's Course class defines the stored property and initializer parameter as `lecturer`. Meanwhile the solution's Client and Developer code still use `instructor`. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the intended property name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the property and initializer parameter name consistent across all artifacts. Prefer using `instructor` to match the problem statement and the template: rename the Course stored property and initializer parameter from `lecturer` to `instructor`, and update its usages accordingly in Client.swift and Developer.swift. Alternatively, change Client and Developer to use `lecturer` everywhere, but ensure all files use the same name so the code compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The concept of the course teacher is named inconsistently across artifacts: the problem statement and the template refer to the property/parameter as "instructor", while the solution implementation uses the identifier "lecturer" for the same concept. This mismatch breaks the direct mapping students expect between the problem description, the starter code, and the reference solution and may cause confusion when locating or using the course's teacher property.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the course teacher across all artifacts. Prefer using the name from the problem statement and template ("instructor") or update the problem/template to "lecturer". Concretely, change the solution's Course property and initializer parameter from "lecturer" to "instructor", and update all references (e.g., Client.swift and Developer.swift attend(...) print) to use course.instructor.
